candidates.label: First branchial cleft anomaly (type II) with recurrent neck cellulitis and fistulous tract from middle ear to mastoid tip, associated with otomandibular syndrome and temporal bone hypoplasia
missing_or_uncertain: Specific type of first branchial anomaly (type I vs II)

candidates.label: Cholesteatoma of the middle ear with mastoid fistula and recurrent neck infection
missing_or_uncertain: Presence of keratinizing squamous epithelium on histology

candidates.label: Chronic suppurative otitis media with mastoiditis and parapharyngeal abscess
Congenital aural fistula (preauricular or postauricular) with recurrent infection
Branchial cleft cyst (second or third) with infection and fistulization to middle ear
missing_or_uncertain: Anatomic location of cyst relative to branchial arches

response.rationale: The combination of otomandibular syndrome, temporal bone hypoplasia, recurrent neck cellulitis, and a fistula from middle ear to mastoid tip strongly indicates a first branchial cleft anomaly. The 2-cm mass is likely an inflammatory or cystic component. Cholesteatoma is less likely given the congenital features and specific fistula location; other branchial anomalies are less consistent with the middle ear origin.
